question.problem:
The birth weights of newborns in a given population are normally distributed with a mean of  $7\,\text{lb}$ and a standard deviation of $0.8\,\text{lb}.$ Suppose $9$ newborn babies are randomly selected. What is the probability that the mean weight for this sample will be more than $7.5\,\text{lb}?$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9599\,$ | $\,0.9608\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ | $\,0.9633\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9678\,$ | $\,0.9686\,$ | $\,0.9693\,$ | $\,0.9699\,$ | $\,0.9706\,$ |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9744\,$ | $\,0.9750\,$ | $\,0.9756\,$ | $\,0.9761\,$ | $\,0.9767\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =7,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =0.8,$ and that the sample size $n=9.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(7,\frac{{0.8}^{2}}{9}) \\  & ∼N\,(7,0.0711).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>7.5).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>7.5) & =P(Z>\frac{7.5-7}{\sqrt{0.0711}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.88) \\  & =1-P(Z<1.88) \\  & =1-Φ(1.88)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.88)=0.9699.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>7.5) & =1-Φ(1.88) \\  & =1-0.9699 \\  & =0.0301\end{aligned}
$$
